[[File:1986 Jeno's Pizza - 15 - Willie Davis (cropped).jpg|thumb|The [[Green Bay Packers|Packers]] defeated the [[Kansas City Chiefs|Chiefs]] in the first [[AFL–NFL World Championship Game]] ([[Super Bowl I]]).]]

The [[Super Bowl]] is the annual [[American football]] game that determines the champion of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). The game culminates a [[National Football League regular season|season]] that begins in the previous calendar year, and is the conclusion of the [[National Football League playoffs|NFL playoffs]]. The winner receives the [[Vince Lombardi Trophy]]. The contest is held in an American city, chosen three to four years beforehand,<ref>{{cite news |last= Forbes |first= Gordon |work=[[USA Today]] |title= The process of choosing a host city |page= 4C |date= November 8, 1990 }}</ref> usually at warm-weather sites or [[Stadium#Types|domed stadiums]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Stellino |first=Vito |date=February 4, 2007 |title=Super Bowl cities are far and few between |url=http://jacksonville.com/tu-online/stories/020407/jag_7751185.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070206022051/http://jacksonville.com/tu-online/stories/020407/jag_7751185.shtml |archive-date=February 6, 2007 |access-date=February 2, 2015 |work=[[The Florida Times-Union]]}}</ref> Since January 1971, the winner of the [[AFC Championship Game|American Football Conference (AFC) Championship Game]] has faced the winner of the [[NFC Championship Game|National Football Conference (NFC) Championship Game]] in the culmination of the NFL playoffs.

Before the [[AFL–NFL merger|1970 merger]] between the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and the NFL, the two leagues met in four such contests. The first two were marketed as the "AFL–NFL World Championship Game", but were also casually referred to as "the Super Bowl game" during the television broadcast.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dVizBENi9cQ#t=27m54s Top Plays in Super Bowl History] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206034103/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dVizBENi9cQ#t=27m54s |date=February 6, 2018 }} "and the old veteran scores the first touchdown of the Super Bowl game" [[YouTube]], [https://www.youtube.com/nfl NFL Highlights] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180215232921/https://www.youtube.com/NFL |date=February 15, 2018 }}.</ref> [[Super Bowl III]] in January 1969 was the first such game that carried the "Super Bowl" moniker in official marketing; the names "[[Super Bowl I]]" and "[[Super Bowl II]]" were retroactively applied to the first two games.<ref name=nflaflwcg>{{cite web |url= http://www.shmoop.com/nfl-history/culture.html |title= Culture in NFL History |website= Shmoop.com |access-date= January 17, 2018 |archive-date= November 22, 2009 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20091122182908/http://www.shmoop.com/nfl-history/culture.html |url-status= live }}</ref> 

A total of 20 franchises, including teams that have relocated to another city or changed their name, have won the Super Bowl.<ref name=record>{{cite web |work= [[NFL.com]] |url= http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/history |title= Super Bowl History |access-date= January 13, 2008 |archive-date= February 23, 2011 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110223141027/http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/history |url-status= live }}</ref> There are four [[NFL team]]s that have never appeared in a Super Bowl: the [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Detroit Lions]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], and [[Houston Texans]], though both the Browns ([[1950 NFL Championship Game|1950]], [[1954 NFL Championship Game|1954]], [[1955 NFL Championship Game|1955]], [[1964 NFL Championship Game|1964]]) and Lions ([[1935 NFL Championship Game|1935]], [[1952 NFL Championship Game|1952]], [[1953 NFL Championship Game|1953]], [[1957 NFL Championship Game|1957]]) had won [[NFL Championship Game]]s prior to the creation of the Super Bowl in the [[1966 NFL season|1966 season]]. 

The [[1972 Miami Dolphins season|1972 Miami Dolphins]] capped off the only [[perfect season]] in [[history of the National Football League|NFL history]] with their victory in [[Super Bowl VII]]. Only two franchises have ever won the Super Bowl while hosting at their home stadiums: the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in [[Super Bowl LV]] and the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in [[Super Bowl LVI]]. The reigning champions are the [[Seattle Seahawks]] following their victory over the [[New England Patriots]] in [[Super Bowl LX]].

* '''Venue''' column indicates number of times that stadium has hosted a Super Bowl.
* '''City''' column indicates number of times that metropolitan area has hosted a Super Bowl.

==Streaks and rematches==
===Consecutive wins===
[[File:1986 Jeno's Pizza - 46 - Terry Bradshaw (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|The [[Pittsburgh Steelers|Steelers]] defeated the [[Los Angeles Rams|Rams]] in [[Super Bowl XIV]] to win an unprecedented four championships in six years.]]

Eight franchises have won consecutive Super Bowls, one of which (Pittsburgh) has accomplished it twice:

* [[Green Bay Packers]] (Super Bowls [[Super Bowl I|I]] and [[Super Bowl II|II]])
* [[Miami Dolphins]] ([[Super Bowl VII|VII]] and [[Super Bowl VIII|VIII]])
* [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] (twice: [[Super Bowl IX|IX]] and [[Super Bowl X|X]]; [[Super Bowl XIII|XIII]] and [[Super Bowl XIV|XIV]])
* [[San Francisco 49ers]] ([[Super Bowl XXIII|XXIII]] and [[Super Bowl XXIV|XXIV]])
* [[Dallas Cowboys]] ([[Super Bowl XXVII|XXVII]] and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|XXVIII]])
* [[Denver Broncos]] ([[Super Bowl XXXII|XXXII]] and [[Super Bowl XXXIII|XXXIII]])<ref group=n name=BroncosStreaks />
* [[New England Patriots]] ([[Super Bowl XXXVIII|XXXVIII]] and [[Super Bowl XXXIX|XXXIX]])
* [[Kansas City Chiefs]] ([[Super Bowl LVII|LVII]] and [[Super Bowl LVIII|LVIII]])

Although no franchise to date has won three Super Bowls in a row, several have had eras of sustained success, nearly accomplishing a [[three-peat]]:

* The [[Green Bay Packers]] won the first two Super Bowls, and also won the [[1965 NFL Championship Game|NFL Championship Game the preceding year]]. If the Super Bowl had been instituted that year, the Packers would have qualified and faced the Buffalo Bills of the AFL.
* The [[Miami Dolphins]] appeared in three consecutive Super Bowls ([[Super Bowl VI|VI]], [[Super Bowl VII|VII]], and [[Super Bowl VIII|VIII]])&nbsp;– winning the last two.
* The [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] won two consecutive Super Bowls ([[Super Bowl IX|IX]] and [[Super Bowl X|X]]); they also won two more consecutive Super Bowls ([[Super Bowl XIII|XIII]] and [[Super Bowl XIV|XIV]]) for four titles in six seasons.
* The [[Dallas Cowboys]] won two consecutive Super Bowls ([[Super Bowl XXVII|XXVII]] and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|XXVIII]]); the [[1995 Dallas Cowboys season|Cowboys]] won [[Super Bowl XXX]] the following year for three titles in four seasons.
* The [[New England Patriots]] won Super Bowls [[Super Bowl XLIX|XLIX]], [[Super Bowl LI|LI]], and [[Super Bowl LIII|LIII]] for three titles in five seasons. They also appeared in and lost [[Super Bowl LII]] to the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] following the 2017 season, giving them four Super Bowl appearances in five years.
* The [[Kansas City Chiefs]] came the closest to a three-peat, winning back-to-back Super Bowls in [[Super Bowl LVII|LVII]] and [[Super Bowl LVIII|LVIII]] but losing their third consecutive appearance in [[Super Bowl LIX|LIX]]. They additionally won [[Super Bowl LIV|LIV]] several years beforehand, and lost [[Super Bowl LV|LV]], for a total of five Super Bowl appearances in six seasons.

===Consecutive losses===
Three franchises have lost consecutive Super Bowls:
* [[Buffalo Bills]] (4) (Super Bowls [[Super Bowl XXV|XXV]], [[Super Bowl XXVI|XXVI]], [[Super Bowl XXVII|XXVII]], and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|XXVIII]]) – The only team to appear in four straight Super Bowls; they lost in all four appearances.
* [[Minnesota Vikings]] (2) ([[Super Bowl VIII|VIII]] and [[Super Bowl IX|IX]]) – They also lost [[Super Bowl XI]], and were [[1975–76 NFL playoffs#NFC: Dallas Cowboys 17, Minnesota Vikings 14|knocked out of the 1975–76 playoffs]] by the eventual [[Super Bowl X]] losers, [[1975 Dallas Cowboys season|the Dallas Cowboys]], for three losses in four seasons.
* [[Denver Broncos]] (2) ([[Super Bowl XXI|XXI]] and [[Super Bowl XXII|XXII]]) – They also lost [[Super Bowl XXIV]], but did not qualify for the [[1988–89 NFL playoffs|1988–89 playoffs]] for [[Super Bowl XXIII]] for three losses in four seasons.<ref group=n name=BroncosStreaks />

===Consecutive appearances===
The [[Buffalo Bills]] have the most consecutive appearances with four from 1990 to 1993. The [[Miami Dolphins]] (1971–1973), [[New England Patriots]] (2016–2018) and [[Kansas City Chiefs]] (2022–2024) are the only other teams to have at least three consecutive appearances. Including those four, 12 teams have at least two consecutive appearances. The [[Dallas Cowboys]] are the only team with three separate streaks (1970–1971, 1977–1978, and 1992–1993). The [[Green Bay Packers]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Denver Broncos]], New England Patriots, and Kansas City Chiefs have each had two separate consecutive appearances. The full listing of teams with consecutive appearances is below in order of first occurrence; winning games are in '''bold''':
* [[Green Bay Packers]] (twice: Super Bowls [[Super Bowl I|'''I''']] and [[Super Bowl II|'''II''']]; [[Super Bowl XXXI|'''XXXI''']] and [[Super Bowl XXXII|XXXII]])
* [[Dallas Cowboys]] (thrice: [[Super Bowl V|V]] and [[Super Bowl VI|'''VI''']]; [[Super Bowl XII|'''XII''']] and [[Super Bowl XIII|XIII]]; [[Super Bowl XXVII|'''XXVII''']] and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|'''XXVIII''']])
* [[Miami Dolphins]] ([[Super Bowl VI|VI]], [[Super Bowl VII|'''VII''']], and [[Super Bowl VIII|'''VIII''']])
* [[Minnesota Vikings]] ([[Super Bowl VIII|VIII]] and [[Super Bowl IX|IX]])
* [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] (twice: [[Super Bowl IX|'''IX''']] and [[Super Bowl X|'''X''']]; [[Super Bowl XIII|'''XIII''']] and [[Super Bowl XIV|'''XIV''']])
* [[Washington Redskins]] ([[Super Bowl XVII|'''XVII''']] and [[Super Bowl XVIII|XVIII]])
* [[Denver Broncos]] (twice: [[Super Bowl XXI|XXI]] and [[Super Bowl XXII|XXII]]; [[Super Bowl XXXII|'''XXXII''']] and [[Super Bowl XXXIII|'''XXXIII''']])<ref group=n name=BroncosStreaks>The [[Denver Broncos|Broncos]] are the only NFL team with both consecutive wins and consecutive losses at the [[Super Bowl]].</ref>
* [[San Francisco 49ers]] ([[Super Bowl XXIII|'''XXIII''']] and [[Super Bowl XXIV|'''XXIV''']])
* [[Buffalo Bills]] ([[Super Bowl XXV|XXV]], [[Super Bowl XXVI|XXVI]], [[Super Bowl XXVII|XXVII]], and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|XXVIII]])
* [[New England Patriots]] (twice: [[Super Bowl XXXVIII|'''XXXVIII''']] and [[Super Bowl XXXIX|'''XXXIX''']]; [[Super Bowl LI|'''LI''']], [[Super Bowl LII|LII]], and [[Super Bowl LIII|'''LIII''']])
* [[Seattle Seahawks]] ([[Super Bowl XLVIII|'''XLVIII''']] and [[Super Bowl XLIX|XLIX]])
* [[Kansas City Chiefs]] (twice: [[Super Bowl LIV|'''LIV''']] and [[Super Bowl LV|LV]]; [[Super Bowl LVII|'''LVII''']], [[Super Bowl LVIII|'''LVIII''']], and [[Super Bowl LIX|LIX]])

===Super Bowl rematches===
[[File:1986 Jeno's Pizza - 27 - Dan Bunz (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|The [[San Francisco 49ers|49ers]] and the [[Cincinnati Bengals|Bengals]], who faced off in [[Super Bowl XVI]] (''pictured''), would play each other again in [[Super Bowl XXIII]].]]
The following teams have faced each other more than once in the Super Bowl:{{#tag:ref|The [[New York Jets]] and [[Baltimore Colts|Baltimore]]/[[Indianapolis Colts]] ([[Super Bowl III]]) is the only [[Super Bowl]] matchup that cannot be repeated under the current playoff alignment, as the Colts have since been placed in the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] (at the time, along with all of the former [[American Football League|AFL]] teams, including the Jets) as part of the [[AFL–NFL merger]] in 1970. For the same reason, it is the only Super Bowl rematch that is capable of being played in the postseason outside of the Super Bowl.|group=n|name=ImpossibleRematch}}
* 3 times – [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] ([[Super Bowl X|X]] and [[Super Bowl XIII|XIII]]) vs. [[Dallas Cowboys]] ([[Super Bowl XXX|XXX]]) – ''see also [[Cowboys–Steelers rivalry]]''
* 2 times – [[Miami Dolphins]] ([[Super Bowl VII|VII]]) vs. [[Washington Redskins]] ([[Super Bowl XVII|XVII]])
* 2 times – [[San Francisco 49ers]] ([[Super Bowl XVI|XVI]] and [[Super Bowl XXIII|XXIII]]) vs. [[Cincinnati Bengals]]
* 2 times – [[Dallas Cowboys]] ([[Super Bowl XXVII|XXVII]] and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|XXVIII]]) vs. [[Buffalo Bills]]{{#tag:ref|The [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Buffalo Bills]] are the only NFL teams to face each other in consecutive [[Super Bowl]]s, [[Super Bowl XXVII|XXVII]] and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|XXVIII]].|group=n|name=ConsecutiveRematch}}
* 2 times – [[New York Giants]] ([[Super Bowl XLII|XLII]] and [[Super Bowl XLVI|XLVI]]) vs. [[New England Patriots]] – ''see also [[Giants–Patriots rivalry]]''
* 2 times –  [[New England Patriots]]  ([[Super Bowl XXXIX|XXXIX]]) vs. [[Philadelphia Eagles]] ([[Super Bowl LII|LII]])
* 2 times –  [[New England Patriots]]  ([[Super Bowl XXXVI|XXXVI]] and [[Super Bowl LIII|LIII]]) vs. [[St. Louis Rams|St. Louis]] / [[Los Angeles Rams]]{{#tag:ref|This is the only rematch pairing in which one team [[National Football League franchise moves and mergers|relocated]] in the interim. The Rams represented St. Louis in [[Super Bowl XXXVI]] and Los Angeles in [[Super Bowl LIII]].|group=n|name=Relocated}}
* 2 times – [[Kansas City Chiefs]] ([[Super Bowl LIV|LIV]] and [[Super Bowl LVIII|LVIII]]) vs. [[San Francisco 49ers]]
* 2 times – [[Kansas City Chiefs]] ([[Super Bowl LVII|LVII]]) vs. [[Philadelphia Eagles]] ([[Super Bowl LIX|LIX]])
* 2 times – [[New England Patriots]] ([[Super Bowl XLIX|XLIX]]) vs. [[Seattle Seahawks]] ([[Super Bowl LX|LX]])

[[File:1986 Jeno's Pizza - 11 - Jim McMahon (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|The New England Patriots played their first championship game in [[Super Bowl XX]] (''pictured'') where they lost to the [[Chicago Bears|Bears]]. This is the most recent [[Super Bowl]] where both teams had their first Super Bowl appearance. The Patriots hold the record for most Super Bowl appearances (12) and most losses (6) while being tied with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers|Steelers]] for most wins (6).]]<!--Deliberately not in the below section as it is more relevant in this one. It is placed below the table so that the width of the table isn't excessively shrunk.-->

===Teams with Super Bowl appearances but no victories===
Eight teams have appeared in the Super Bowl without ever winning. In descending order of number of appearances and then years since their last appearance, they are:
* [[Minnesota Vikings]] (4) – appeared in Super Bowls [[Super Bowl IV|IV]], [[Super Bowl VIII|VIII]], [[Super Bowl IX|IX]], and [[Super Bowl XI|XI]]; they won the [[1969 NFL Championship Game|NFL Championship]] in [[1969 NFL season|1969]], the last year before the [[AFL–NFL merger]], but failed to win [[Super Bowl IV|the subsequent Super Bowl]]. 
* [[Buffalo Bills]] (4) – [[Super Bowl XXV|XXV]], [[Super Bowl XXVI|XXVI]], [[Super Bowl XXVII|XXVII]], and [[Super Bowl XXVIII|XXVIII]]; in [[1964 AFL season|1964]] and [[1965 AFL season|1965]], they won the [[1964 American Football League Championship Game|last]] [[1965 American Football League Championship Game|two]] AFL Championships before the [[Super Bowl I|first Super Bowl]] in [[1966 AFL season|1966]].
* [[Cincinnati Bengals]] (3) – [[Super Bowl XVI|XVI]], [[Super Bowl XXIII|XXIII]], and [[Super Bowl LVI|LVI]]; an AFL expansion team in [[1968 Cincinnati Bengals season|1968]], they have no pre-Super Bowl league championships.
* [[Carolina Panthers]] (2) – [[Super Bowl XXXVIII|XXXVIII]] and [[Super Bowl 50|50]]; a post-merger expansion team, their first season was in [[1995 Carolina Panthers season|1995]].
* [[Atlanta Falcons]] (2) – [[Super Bowl XXXIII|XXXIII]] and [[Super Bowl LI|LI]]; an NFL expansion team in [[1966 Atlanta Falcons season|1966]], they have no pre-Super Bowl league championships.
* [[Los Angeles Chargers]] (1) – [[Super Bowl XXIX|XXIX]] as the [[History of the San Diego Chargers|San Diego Chargers]]; their only [[1963 American Football League Championship Game|AFL Championship]] was in [[1963 AFL season|1963]], also as the San Diego Chargers.
* [[Tennessee Titans]] (1) – [[Super Bowl XXXIV|XXXIV]]; they won the [[1960 American Football League Championship Game|first]] [[1961 American Football League Championship Game|two]] AFL Championships in [[1960 AFL season|1960]] and [[1961 AFL season|1961]] as the [[History of the Houston Oilers|Houston Oilers]].
* [[Arizona Cardinals]] (1) – [[Super Bowl XLIII|XLIII]]; they won two [[1947 NFL Championship Game|NFL Championship]]s, one in [[1925 NFL season|1925]] and then again in [[1947 NFL season|1947]], both as the [[History of the Chicago Cardinals|Chicago Cardinals]].

===Teams with no Super Bowl appearances or long active droughts===
[[File:1986 Jeno's Pizza - 37 - Joe Namath (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|The [[New York Jets|Jets]]' most recent championship appearance was their victory over the [[Baltimore Colts|Colts]] in [[Super Bowl III]].]]
Four current teams have never reached the Super Bowl (shown in '''bold''' below). Two of them (Jacksonville and Houston) joined the NFL relatively recently, and there are an additional eight teams whose Super Bowl appearance droughts began prior to [[2002 NFL season|2002]] (the year Houston joined the NFL). The other two teams that have never appeared in a Super Bowl (Cleveland and Detroit) both held [[List of NFL champions (1920–69)|NFL league championships]] prior to [[Super Bowl I]] in the [[1966 NFL season]].{{#tag:ref|[[Detroit]], [[Houston]], and [[Jacksonville]] have all hosted [[Super Bowl]]s, making [[Cleveland]] the only current NFL city that has neither hosted nor had its team play in a Super Bowl.|group=n|name=NFLCityNoSB}}  Teams are listed below according to the length of their current Super Bowl droughts (as of the end of the [[2025 NFL season|2025 season]]):
* '''[[Cleveland Browns]]''', 60 years{{#tag:ref|The Browns are officially viewed as one continuous franchise that began in [[1946 Cleveland Browns season|1946]] as a member of the [[All-America Football Conference]], [[AAFC–NFL merger|joined the NFL]] in [[1950 Cleveland Browns season|1950]], suspended operations after [[1995 Cleveland Browns season|1995]], and resumed play in [[1999 Cleveland Browns season|1999]].|name=Cleveland Browns|group=n}} – NFL champions four times in [[1950 NFL Championship Game|1950]], [[1954 NFL Championship Game|1954]], [[1955 NFL Championship Game|1955]], and [[1964 NFL Championship Game|1964]]; appeared in seven other [[List of NFL champions (1920–1969)|NFL Championship Games]] in [[1951 NFL Championship Game|1951]], [[1952 NFL Championship Game|1952]], [[1953 NFL Championship Game|1953]], [[1957 NFL Championship Game|1957]], [[1965 NFL Championship Game|1965]], [[1968 NFL Championship Game|1968]], and [[1969 NFL Championship Game|1969]]; and appeared in three [[AFC Championship Game]]s in the [[1986–87 NFL playoffs#AFC: Denver Broncos 23, Cleveland Browns 20 (OT)|1986]], [[1987–88 NFL playoffs#AFC: Denver Broncos 38, Cleveland Browns 33|1987]], and [[1989–90 NFL playoffs#AFC: Denver Broncos 37, Cleveland Browns 21|1989]] seasons.<ref name="BrownsResults">{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns Franchise Encyclopedia |website=Pro Football Reference |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cle/ |access-date=August 27, 2009 |archive-date=October 18, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018094523/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cle/ |url-status=live|publisher=Sports Reference LLC}}</ref>
* '''[[Detroit Lions]]''', 60 years – NFL champions four times in [[1935 NFL Championship Game|1935]], [[1952 NFL Championship Game|1952]], [[1953 NFL Championship Game|1953]], and [[1957 NFL Championship Game|1957]]; appeared in one other [[List of NFL champions (1920–1969)|NFL Championship Game]] in [[1954 NFL Championship Game|1954]]; and  appeared in two [[NFC Championship Game|NFC Championship Games]] in the [[1991–92 NFL playoffs#NFC: Washington Redskins 41, Detroit Lions 10|1991]] and [[2023 NFL season|2023 season]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions Franchise Encyclopedia |website=Pro Football Reference |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/det/ |access-date=August 27, 2009 |archive-date=October 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201004011702/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/det/ |url-status=live|publisher=Sports Reference LLC}}</ref>
* [[New York Jets]], 57 years – Won [[Super Bowl III]], [[1968 American Football League season|1968 season]]<ref>{{Cite web |last= Neumann |first= Thomas |title= Page 2's ultimate NFL power rankings, Nos. 21–32 |work= [[ESPN]] |publisher= [[The Walt Disney Company]] |date= September 17, 2008 |url= https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=nflrankings/21-32/080917 |access-date= September 7, 2009 |archive-date= February 7, 2009 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090207143055/http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/page2/story?page=nflrankings/21-32/080917 |url-status= live }}</ref>{{#tag:ref|The [[New York Jets|Jets]] and the [[Kansas City Chiefs|Chiefs]] are the only teams to win the [[Super Bowl]] as members of the now-defunct [[American Football League|AFL]]. The Jets have not appeared in the Super Bowl since joining the NFL following the [[AFL–NFL merger]] in 1970.|group=n|name=nonNFLSBChampions}}
* [[Minnesota Vikings]], 49 years – Lost [[Super Bowl XI]], [[1976 NFL season|1976 season]]
* [[Miami Dolphins]], 41 years – Lost [[Super Bowl XIX]], [[1984 NFL season|1984 season]]
* [[Washington Commanders]], 34 years – Won [[Super Bowl XXVI]], [[1991 NFL season|1991 season]] (played as [[History of the Washington Football Team|Washington Redskins]])
* [[Buffalo Bills]], 32 years – Lost [[Super Bowl XXVIII]], [[1993 NFL season|1993 season]]
* [[Los Angeles Chargers]], 31 years – Lost [[Super Bowl XXIX]], [[1994 NFL season|1994 season]] (played as [[History of the San Diego Chargers|San Diego Chargers]])
* '''[[Jacksonville Jaguars]]''', 31 years – [[1995 Jacksonville Jaguars season|1995]] [[expansion team#National Football League|expansion team]]; three [[AFC Championship Game]] appearances in the [[1996–97 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 20, Jacksonville Jaguars 6|1996]], [[1999–2000 NFL playoffs#AFC: Tennessee Titans 33, Jacksonville Jaguars 14|1999]], and [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#AFC Championship Game: New England Patriots 24, Jacksonville Jaguars 20|2017 season]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title= Jacksonville Jaguars Franchise Encyclopedia |website= Pro Football Reference |url= https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/jax/ |access-date= August 27, 2009 |archive-date= January 15, 2016 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160115203217/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/jax/ |url-status= live |publisher=Sports Reference LLC}}</ref>
* [[Dallas Cowboys]], 30 years – Won [[Super Bowl XXX]], [[1995 NFL season|1995 season]]
* [[Tennessee Titans]], 26 years – Lost [[Super Bowl XXXIV]], [[1999 NFL season|1999 season]]
* '''[[Houston Texans]]''', 24 years – [[2002 Houston Texans season|2002]] [[expansion team#National Football League|expansion team]]; [[NFL playoffs#Current playoff system|Divisional Round]] appearances in the [[2011–12 NFL playoffs#AFC: Baltimore Ravens 20, Houston Texans 13|2011]], [[2012–13 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 41, Houston Texans 28|2012]], [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 34, Houston Texans 16|2016]], [[2019–20 NFL playoffs#AFC: Kansas City Chiefs 51, Houston Texans 31|2019]], [[2023 NFL season|2023]], [[2024 NFL season|2024]], and [[2025 NFL season|2025]] seasons. They are the only NFL team to never reach the Conference Championship round.
